### DHCP messages (1)  {.smaller}


* protocol looks weird in packet traces because of history
* built on top of UDP + IP
* built as extension to older BOOTP (bootstrap protocol) 
<hr class="vspace" />
* common message format for different ‘‘operations’’


### DHCP messages (2)  {.smaller}


* from client (looking to configure itself): 

   * DISCOVER (look for configuration server)
   * REQUEST (get configuration from server)

* from server (offering configurations): 

   * OFFER (‘I am a configuration server’)
   * ACK (here's a configuration)



### DHCP request example 



::: {.r-stack .my-full}
![](/arp/texfig/dhcp-dhcp-request-example.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Screenshot of wireshark capture of DHCP request message. The message has several IP address fields which are all set to 0.0.0.0. It also contains the Client MAC address and several 'options': a DHCP message type, client identifier, parameter request list, maximum DHCP message, a requested IP address, and a host name."}

![](/arp/texfig/dhcp-dhcp-request-example.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="The protocol list in Wirehsark is highlighted: Ethernet IIi with dst=ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, IPv4 with src=0.0.0.0 and dst=255.255.255.255, UDP src port=68 and dst port=67."}

![](/arp/texfig/dhcp-dhcp-request-example.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="The 'message type' of 'Boot Request (1)' is highlighted."}

![](/arp/texfig/dhcp-dhcp-request-example.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 fig-alt="The 'Client IP address', 'Your (client) IP address', 'Next server IP address' and 'Relay agent IP address' fields are highlgihted. The corresponding values are all 0.0.0.0"}

:::

::: {.myoverbox .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 .low}

*  built on IP+UDP rather than special protocol like ARP
*  sending to broadcast ethernet/IP address (all 1 bits)
*  placeholder source IP address of 0.0.0.0

:::


::: {.myoverbox .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 .low}

*  `boot' because derived from bootstrap protocol (BOOTP)

:::



::: {.myoverbox .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 .low}

*  message format here is the same in both directions, so fields here are intended for use in response

:::

### DHCP leases 


* DHCP ACKs specify a time limit 

   * (example from prior slide (UVa eduroam): 30 minutes)

* need to be renewed (new REQUEST + ACK) 

   * REQUESTs can contain ‘desired address’ (= current address when renewing)
